invalid_failure_risks: Replay server may not reset state between connections from ref_fingerprint and extractor, causing output sequence divergence unrelated to correctness bugs.
10ms fragmentation delay is potentially flaky under CPU contention in a 1-CPU container — could cause timing-dependent test failures.

The 4-byte length-prefix protocol is described only in the environment spec, not in the solver instruction — solver must reverse-engineer it from the extractor source, which is fair but could cause confusion if extractor is badly broken.

If the corpus.bin GREASE entries only contain 0x0a0a in curves, a solver who fixes both bugs but introduces a subtly different GREASE formula (e.g., checking only high nibble) may pass corpus tests but fail verify-time tests — this is intended, but the verifier must reliably generate 0x1a1a/0x2a2a inputs.

The no-extensions fingerprint format 'SSLVersion,,,,' is stated but if the reference binary emits 'SSLVersion,,,' (three dashes, four fields) vs 'SSLVersion,,,,' (four commas, five fields), there is an off-by-one ambiguity in field count that could cause unresolvable mismatches.
review.reasons: The task has strong verifiability via a reference binary oracle and fuzz equivalence testing with fresh inputs, ensuring hollow partial fixes cannot pass. The two bugs are source-visible in ~14 commands which limits genuine_difficulty to 3, but the corpus trap (0x0a0a only) and misleading struct.unpack symptom provide meaningful agent-failure modes. All scores meet the 3-floor threshold and the 3.6 average (4.2) is satisfied.
fixes: Add an explicit statement in the instruction that GREASE must be stripped from ALL numeric list fields including elliptic curve point formats, to eliminate the ambiguity noted in the expected failure modes.

Ensure the replay server resets its corpus position to the beginning on each new TCP connection (not just continuously streaming), so ref_fingerprint and extractor see identical byte sequences regardless of connection order.

Add one or two ClientHello samples with 0x1a1a or 0x3a3a GREASE in curves to the baked corpus.bin so the broken GREASE check manifests during development, not only at verify time — this makes the difficulty more legitimate (agent must fix it to pass any test) rather than relying on a corpus gap.

Specify in the instruction or README the exact GREASE definition (two-byte value where both bytes are equal and each ends in 0xa, i.e., values 0x0a0a, 0x1a1a, ..., 0xfafa) to avoid ambiguity about what 'correct' GREASE filtering means without the reference binary.
